summary: DPM Financial Services is a Melbourne and Sydney group (since 1964) providing tax, accounting, lending and insurance to doctors. Michael Allsopp became CEO in May 2026 after a COO role at a property consultancy, and the firm is advertising Tax Accountant roles. Its work is tax-compliance and client-advice heavy rather than high-volume monthly closes.

Dino Miliotis is listed on DPM's people page as a Principal in tax at the Melbourne office.

hooks.text: New CEO (since May 2026) with a systems-and-structures-to-scale background; likely interested in operating-model efficiency.
Tax & Accounting already digitalised and hiring Tax Accountants: capacity is a live issue and reconciliation sits upstream of every return.
Work spans trusts, family groups and BAS/IAS, so recurring Xero files exist behind compliance work.

risks.text: Practice is tax-compliance and client-advice focused for doctors, not a volume bookkeeping or monthly close model; weak-to-moderate fit.
CEO is only months into the role and came from property; may be focused on org change before tooling.

gaps: No podcast, video or Facebook/Instagram content by Michael or DPM found.
No explicit mention of reconciliation volume or AI tools.
Third-party LinkedIn lists a former CEO (Linda Pickering) alongside Michael; DPM's own site and Michael's profile confirm Michael as current CEO.
Dino Miliotis's recent public activity not found.

first.subject: Reconciliation inside DPM's tax team
first.body:
Hi Michael, I read your CEO message on the DPM story page about joining in May and finding a strong foundation, and your background building the systems and structures that help private firms scale. DPM has already digitalised its tax and accounting service and is hiring Tax Accountants now. I built Vert to turn hours of manual reconciliation into minutes, with a trail you can trace instead of AI that guesses. For a team preparing returns for family groups and trusts in Xero, how much of each job still starts with reconciling by hand?

Best,
Dawoud
